name: 褐背針尾雨燕

similarSpecies.distinction: Substantive identification/range/conservation read. Sexes similar. Dark blue-gloss brown, PALE SILVERY GREY SADDLE on back, broad sharply contrasting WHITE THROAT plus WHITE LORES/FOREHEAD BAND. White horseshoe rear flanks/undertail around dark belly, short square tail tiny needle spines only close views. caudacutus central Siberia to Sakhalin/Kurils/Mongolia/NE China/Korea/Japan breeding, winters S New Guinea/E Australia; nudipes N Pakistan/Himalaya/N Myanmar/SW China, winter poorly known possibly Malaya/Java. LC stable globally; scarce HK spring migrant declined locally since1990s, not a global IUCN trend.

Substantive identification/range/conservation read. Sexes similar. Dark blue-gloss brown with pale SILVERY GREY SADDLE. ILL-DEFINED DUSKY GREY BROWN THROAT and DARK FOREHEAD unlike white-throated. White horseshoe rear flank/undertail and short square needle-spined tail. Distant birds very hard to separate; close head/throat views important. Monotypic breeds central Nepal/NE India/N Myanmar/S China to E Guangxi/Hainan/Taiwan, winters Thailand/Malay peninsula/Sumatra/W Java. LC stable globally; scarce HK spring passage declined locally since1990s.

rangeMap.note: Adult indicus representation; sexes similar. Long full body long broad wings short square tail, prominent projecting needle spines, white horseshoe lower flanks/undertail. Pale BROWN saddle vs SILVERY GREY congeners; dark brown throat with paler chin close-up, indicus white loral spot. Artwork not guaranteed to accurately illustrate loral position; do not label it as diagnostic evidence. indicus mainly resident SW India/Sri Lanka/Andamans/NE India/Bangladesh/Myanmar/Thailand/Cambodia/Vietnam, some northern birds move S Thai-Malay peninsula. Nominate Malay peninsula/Greater Sundas/Palawan. LC decreasing. HK accidental photographed Po Toi24March2012. Partial native-country overview not whole-country occupancy or complete range; world viewport.
